summary: The UI build is non‑functional: both mobile and desktop runtimes throw JavaScript errors, the primary sign‑up flow cannot locate the email field, and consequently the whole user journey is broken. In addition a number of spec‑driven requirements (design‑token usage, complete state handling, accessible markup, interaction states, and form best‑practices) are missing or only partially implemented. These issues will prevent a production‑grade release until they are addressed.

findings.issue: The sign‑up form does not expose a correctly labelled, focusable email `<input>` (no `id`, `name`, or `autocomplete`). Automation cannot locate the field, causing a timeout at step 3 of the primary flow.
findings.fix: Add a `<label htmlFor="email">Email</label>` and `<input id="email" name="email" type="email" autocomplete="email" required>` with visible error messages. Ensure the input is inside a `<form>` element and that the button’s loading state shows a spinner rather than merely disabling the button.

findings.issue: Runtime console errors appear on both mobile and desktop builds (unhandled exception at line 41:659), preventing the React tree from rendering at all.
findings.fix: Open source maps to locate the originating TypeScript source, fix the offending import/value (e.g., mis‑named export, invalid hook usage, or missing dependency). Re‑run the build and verify that no uncaught errors appear in the console.

findings.issue: Missing UI states: the spec requires loading spinner, field‑level inline errors, server‑error banner, and permission‑denied dialog. The component only renders a static form.
findings.fix:
Introduce component state (e.g., `status: 'idle'|'loading'|'error'|'success'`) and conditionally render the spinner in the submit button, inline `

` messages under each field, a banner for server errors, and a modal for camera permission denial.

findings.issue: Similar to receipt upload, the mileage entry form lacks loading, error, and success UI states, and does not display validation messages inline.
findings.fix: Implement the same state machine as ReceiptUpload, with proper aria‑describedby linking for each input’s error message and a toast on success.

findings.issue: Hard‑coded colors, dimensions and shadows are used (e.g., `background:#0066ff; height:48px;`) instead of the design tokens (`var(--c-primary)`, `var(--size-16)`, etc.).
findings.fix: Replace all static values with the CSS variables defined in the design spec. Verify that the CSS file importing the tokens (`src/index.css`) is loaded globally.

findings.issue: Navigation components lack proper landmarks (`<header>`, `<nav aria-label="Primary navigation">`) and focus‑visible outlines for keyboard users.
findings.fix: Wrap the top bar in `<header>` and the tab bar in `<nav aria-label="Primary navigation">`. Add `:focus-visible { outline: var(--focus-ring); outline-offset: 2px; }` to all interactive elements.

findings.issue: Export buttons do not have `role="button"` and missing `aria-live` for loading state. No loading spinner appears on click.
findings.fix: Add `role="button"` (if using non‑button elements), a spinner component that replaces the label when loading, and `aria-live="polite"` on a status container to announce success/error.

findings.issue: Login form lacks password visibility toggle, password rule hint, and does not prevent silent disable of submit; it only disables the button with no feedback.
findings.fix: Add a show/hide eye icon button with `aria-label="Show password"`/`"Hide password"`. Render password rule text under the field. On submit, replace button label with spinner rather than merely disabling it.

findings.issue: Dashboard does not render all required states (loading spinner with aria‑live, empty state CTA, offline banner). The per‑month bar chart is missing a fallback for zero data.
findings.fix: Implement conditional rendering for each state per spec, include `role="status"` with live region for loading, and a top banner `<div role="alert"` for offline notice.

findings.issue: Images (e.g., receipt thumbnails, hero.png) are inserted without meaningful `alt` attributes.
findings.fix: Add descriptive `alt` text derived from receipt metadata, e.g., `alt="Receipt from Acme Corp – 2023‑09‑15"`.

findings.issue: Form inputs miss `autocomplete` attributes (e.g., `autocomplete="off"` on numeric fields, missing on email/password).
findings.fix: Add appropriate `autocomplete` values (`email`, `new-password`, `current-password`, `off` for numeric/date fields).

findings.issue: Input fields are missing native `required` attributes, causing inconsistent native validation.
findings.fix: Add `required` attribute to all mandatory fields.

findings.issue: Some `<button>` elements are missing explicit `type="button"` or `type="submit"`, which can cause unexpected form submissions when nested.
Dialog components lack `role="dialog"`, `aria-modal="true"`, and focus‑trap logic.
findings.fix: Wrap modal markup with `role="dialog" aria-modal="true" aria-labelledby="dialog-title"` and implement a focus trap (e.g., using `react-focus-lock`).

findings.issue: The screen is entirely blank with no UI elements, text, or interactive components visible.
findings.fix: Implement the sign-up form with email, password, and 'Create account' button as specified in the design spec. Ensure proper spacing, typography, and visual hierarchy. Add error states and loading states as defined.

findings.issue: visual quality 1/10 on 'sign-up' (needs 8+): The screen is completely blank — no UI elements, no text, no form, no button, no placeholder, no error state, no empty state message. This is not a usable or even a previewable screen. It violates the core requirement of a sign-up screen to collect user credentials and create an account. A blank screen is a critical failure for any product, especially one that must be paid for and used by real users.
findings.fix: Address this screen's findings until it looks polished and professional.
